{"content": "## Creating a Google Cloud Compute Engine Instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS

> **Note**: Google Cloud does not currently offer the NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU. The closest available GPU types are the NVIDIA Tesla A100, V100, P100, T4, etc. If you specifically need an RTX A6000, you would have to use a different provider (e.g., AWS with `g4dn.xlarge` or `p4d.24xlarge`).

Below is a step‑by‑step guide to create a Compute Engine instance using the **gcloud CLI** and the **REST API**. Replace placeholders (`<PROJECT_ID>`, `<ZONE>`, etc.) with your own values.

---

### 1. Prerequisites

| Requirement | How to satisfy it |
|-------------|-------------------|
| Google Cloud SDK | Install from https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install |
| Billing enabled | Ensure your project has billing attached |
| Compute Engine API enabled | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| GPU API enabled | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` (GPU support is part of Compute Engine) |
| Appropriate IAM permissions | `roles/compute.admin` or `roles/owner` |

---

### 2. Using the gcloud CLI

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT_ID="<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # choose a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"   # replace with the closest available GPU
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
# Note: Replace GPU_TYPE with the actual GPU type you want (e.g., nvidia-tesla-a100)
# If you truly need RTX A6000, you cannot do it on GCP.

gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=$MACHINE_TYPE \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --image-family=$IMAGE_FAMILY \
  --image-project=$IMAGE_PROJECT \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

#### Explanation of flags
| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Attach GPU(s) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Base OS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a script on first boot |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keep the instance running during maintenance |

---

### 3. Using the REST API

Below is a sample **POST** request to the Compute Engine REST API. You can send this via `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client.

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances
Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/<ZONE>/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {"type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\necho 'Hello, world!' > /var/log/startup.log"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

#### Steps to execute
1. **Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token** with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`. You can get one via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` or by using a service account.
2. Replace `<PROJECT_ID>`, `<ZONE>`, and `<ACCESS_TOKEN>` with your actual values.
3. Adjust the `acceleratorType` to the GPU you want. If you truly need RTX A6000, you cannot do it on GCP.
4. Run the request.

---

### 4. Verifying the Instance

After creation, you can verify the instance via:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=$ZONE
```

Look for the `guestAccelerators` section to confirm the GPU attachment.

---

### 5. Cleaning Up

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=$ZONE --quiet
```

---

### 6. Alternative: Using Terraform

If you prefer infrastructure-as-code, here's a minimal Terraform snippet:

```hcl
provider "google" {
  project = "<PROJECT_ID>"
  region  = "us-central1"
}

resource "google_compute_instance" "rtx_a6000" {
  name         = "rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
  machine_type = "n1-standard-8"
  zone         = "us-central1-a"

  boot_disk {
    initialize_params {
      image = "ubuntu-os-cloud/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      size_gb = 100
    }
  }

  guest_accelerator {
    type  = "nvidia-tesla-a100"
    count = 1
  }

  network_interface {
    network = "default"
    access_config {}
  }
}
```

Run `terraform init` and `terraform apply`.

---

### 7. Summary

* Google Cloud does **not** provide RTX A6000 GPUs.
* Use the closest available GPU (e.g., Tesla A100) or switch providers.
* The gcloud CLI and REST API examples above show how to attach a GPU to an Ubuntu 20.04 LTS instance.

Happy computing!", "filename": "create-gcp-instance.md"}

function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.
